title: Publish the Teaching Assistant & Peer Tutoring Operations Playbook for Large University Cohorts, by Fri 11 Dec
description:
Large university STEM departments (150–500+ students per cohort) rely heavily on graduate Teaching Assistants (TAs) and peer tutors to run weekly breakout lab sections, grade problem sets, and triage student inquiries. Instructors currently face student grade leaks and unmoderated discussions when using fragmented group chats. This blueprint establishes Zedu as the secure operating system for university TA and tutorial workflows.

Work under this goal:
- Design the multi-tier university course workspace hierarchy: private TA coordination channels (#ta-backchannel, #grading-rubrics), breakout lab pod channels (#lab-section-01, #lab-section-02), and central professor announcements (#course-notices).
- Write the weekly TA office-hour and live code walkthrough protocol using native Zedu Buzz sessions with screen-sharing toggles.
- Standardize the assignment triage and regrade inquiry guidelines utilizing Zedu's 440px discussion thread drawer to keep grading disputes private and organized.
- Draft the TA onboarding checklist and student lab attendance logging template formatted for Zedu File Management.

Done when: A comprehensive operations kit is delivered with exact channel permission steps for TAs vs professors vs students, TA office-hour agendas, lab thread templates, and file sharing rules verified against live zedu-fe controls.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Map TA duties to Zedu's real roles (owner, admin, member, guest), and keep grades out of chat entirely
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Zedu's workspace roles in the code are owner, admin, member and guest; there's no TA or instructor role. Approach: map each TA duty (run a lab section channel, answer questions, moderate) to the smallest role that allows it, and list the duties that would need admin rights, which affect the whole workspace. To prevent grade leaks, grades are never posted in channels or DMs and stay in the university's LMS, with Zedu used for questions and announcements only. Done: the duty-to-role table with what each role can do (verified in the app), the grade rule, and the section channel layout for a 300-student course.

upvotes.reason: "Map TA duties to Zedu's real roles (owner, admin, member, guest), and keep grades out of chat entirely" gives the team evidence it can act on, with every claim carrying its source, so the result holds up when someone checks it. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.
Mapping TA duties to owner, admin, member and guest, and keeping grades out of chat, avoids inventing a role the product does not have.
Mapping TA duties to the actual owner, admin, member and guest roles prevents a playbook that assumes a role the product does not have, and keeps grades out of chat.

This gives universities a practical role map based on Zedu's actual permission levels and avoids treating the app like a grading system. Verifying each duty before recommending a role protects student records and prevents overstating what a TA can do.
TAs fail in large cohorts when the playbook assumes permissions the role does not have. Mapping each duty to an existing role keeps it executable.
